newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to propose pension reform law.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to propose pension reform law.

text.p: President Bill Clinton was expected to announce on Monday that the U.S. pension watchdog had its first surplus in its 22-year history last year and to propose tighter audits of pension plans, a U.S. official said.

The official, who asked not to be identifed, said Clinton would highlight the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation's (PBGC) annual report to Congress, which shows a surplus of assets over liabilities of $869 million.
It was the first time since the founding of the PBGC, a federal agency that insures private pension plans for millions of Americans, had shown a surplus, the official added.
The report shows PBGC assets of $12.04 billion and liabilities of $11.17 billion for fiscal year 1996, which ended on Sept. 30, 1996.

While saying part of the improved PBGC financial position reflected robust U.S. economic growth, the official argued it was also the result of the administration's efforts to manage the agency better as well as pension reforms passed in 1994.

In addition, the official said the president would use the occasion to put forward ideas to improve pension protections and to resubmit legislation he sent Congress last year that aims to ensure "private pension funds have meaningful audits."

Among the ideas Clinton was expected to announce were a toll-free number for information on pension protections and executive action requiring companies to invest worker pension contributions immediately, rather than pocketing the interest, the official said.

The separate legislative proposal on auditing, which did not make it to a vote when first sent to Congress, is one of a string of small-bore initiatives that marked Clinton's 1996 run for the presidency and the start of his second term.

Last week, Clinton announced a series of similarly limited proposals in the area of health care, naming a commission to monitor health care quality, announcing ideas to crack down on fraud in the Medicare and Medicaid programs, and seeking to expand the availability of mammograms to women over 40.
